$headers = [
     'AccountReference' => 'your-AccountReference-header-here',
     'X-Api-Key' => 'YOUR_KEY_HERE'
    ];

curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, $headers);


    $body = json_encode([
  "throttleScheduleInformation" => [
    "startDate" => "startDate",
    "timeSlotStart" => "string",
    "timeSlotEnd" => "string",
    "endDate" => "endDate",
    "rateOfSend" => 0,
    "daysOfWeek" => [
      ""
    ]
  ],
  "dispatch" => [
    "name" => "name",
    "characterSet" => "characterSet",
    "channel" => "channel",
    "from" => "from",
    "messageType" => "messageType",
    "body" => [
      "text" => "text",
      "templateId" => "templateId"
    ],
    "metaData" => new stdClass()
  ],
  "recipients" => [
    [
      "msisdn" => "msisdn",
      "variables" => new stdClass(),
      "metaData" => new stdClass()

]);
        
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, true);

curl_close($ch);

if ($info['http_code'] >= 400) {

} else {
    echo 'Success! Response: ' . $response;
}

sections.title: API overview
sections.content:
This API enables you to create a batch message request and then control the throughput so not all messages are sent at the same time. This can be configured to splitting messages into hourly batches, or setting a maximum number of messages to be sent within a timeframe i.e. that day.

Not only does throttling for large batch sends ensure that networks don’t become overwhelmed by large requests, it also allows you to better determine the spread of inbound messaging received from a large outbound message.
There are 2 types of throttling methods available via this API:
  • Rate based - control the rate limit of messages to be sent per hour. The platform will then calculate the estimated end date for the request based on the specified rate limit *
  • Period based - specify the end date required for all the messages within the request to be sent. The platform then determines the optimal rate limit for the request

*any throttling schedules applied will still adhere to our default API rate limiting policy. All schedule times should be provided in UTC.
Note: once all messages within a thottled schedule have all been accepted to the platform, the throttle schedule will no longer be editable.

If you would like to duplicate a previous throttled schedule, send a GET request using v2/throttle-schedule/{throttleScheduleId} endpoint to gain the required information. If you're missing the throttle-scheduleId for the request you'd like to duplicate, you can view all throttle schedules by calling GET v2/throttle-schedule. The response data can then be copied to a new POST request as required using v2/throttle-schedule.

Before you start using this endpoint, please check you have your Account, API Key and Base URL set up and have familiarised yourself with our implementation prerequisites in our Introduction documentation.

Please note: some countries have specific sending regulations, visit our support site for further information on territory specific regulations. You can set up your SenderIds, STOP/CONTACT auto-responses for French recipients and other regulation configurations in the Esendex portal.

sections.title: Headers
sections.content:
These parameters are mandatory to be provided in the header of your request. If not provided, or incorrect, your request will fail.

HeaderTypeDescription
Content-TypeStringapplication/json
X-API-KeyStringAPI Key for authorization
AccountReferenceStringYour Esendex account reference - e.g. SPNL000000


Example request header
POST https://api.spryng.nl/v2/throttle-schedule
-H 'Api-Key: YOUR_API_KEY'
-H 'Content-Type: application/json'
-H 'AccountReference: SPNL000000'

sections.title: Request body
sections.content:
You can use the cURL sample provided on the right hand side of this page to directly copy/paste into your chosen integration tool, using the below properties to modify your request as required for your business needs.

Required, or conditional, request body parameters

If a required parameter is not provided, or incorrect, the request will fail. If a parameter is Conditional, it is only required for certain channels or is dependent on the desired format of the message.

Parameter nameTypeRequired or ConditionalDescription
throttleScheduleInformationJSON objectRequiredThe details of the throttled schedule. Use the below properties to define the schedule requirements alongside the conditional properties required depending on if you’re creating a periodic or rate based schedule
throttleScheduleInformation.startDateStringRequiredThe start date of the throttle schedule e.g. “YYYY-MM-DD”
throttleScheduleInformation.timeSlotStartDateStringRequiredThe time the message should be sent provided in ICT format format YYYY-MM-DD:HH:MMZ e.g. 2025-03-05T11:47:25.723Z. The platform operates in UTC time zone exclusively. If you want to schedule a message to correspond to a different time zone
throttleScheduleInformation.rateOfsendIntegerConditionalThe number of messages to be sent per hour. Required if configuring a rate limited scheduled send
throttleScheduleInformation.endDateStringConditionalThe end date of the throttle schedule e.g. “YYYY-MM-DD”. Required if configuring a periodic scheduled send
throttleScheduleInformation.timeSlotEndStringConditionalThe end time of the throttle schedule e.g. “HH:MM:SS”. Must be provided in UTC. Required if configuring a periodic scheduled send
dispatchJSON objectRequiredThe details of the dispatch settings. Use the below properties to define as required
recipientsJSON arrayConditionalThe list of recipients for the message request provided as either a list of recipient numbers or by using existing contacts within your address book
recipients.msisdnStringConditionalThe phone number of recipient
contactsJSON arrayConditionalCan contain an array of contacts. Each contact must correspond to a contactId that belongs to the account which is sending the message. Using contactIds allow the data in each contact's custom fields to be used as variables in the message body
cotacts.contactIdJSON arrayConditionalRequired when using "contacts". The contactId of the contact(s) you wish to send a message to. A max of 50000 contacts can be included in a single request

Optional request body parameters

These parameters are not mandatory within the request body, they are designed to provide you further capability to customise or filter your requests.

ParameterTypeDescription
throttleScheduleInformation.daysOfweekJSON arrayA list of days of the week throttled messages can be sent on. Possible values: Sunday | Monday | Tuesday | Wednesday | Thursday | Friday | Saturday
dispatch.characterSetStringAllowed character sets are: Auto | GSM | Unicode e.g.GSM uses a smaller characterSet which allows characters per message part to around 140. Unicode allows using of a large set of special characters and Unicode emojis but reduces characters per message part to around 70. Auto means we will detect the characters provided and use GSM when only GSM characters are present
dispatch.messageTypeStringUsed to help reporting on certain message types. Enum e.g. MarketingAndResearch | NotificationsAndReminders | AuthenticationAndSecurity | PaymentsAndCollections | InternalOperations | CustomerSupport | Conversational
dispatch.nameStringOptional friendly name for the request. Will be present message history export and can make some data analysis or grouping easier
metaDataJSON objectCan contain "key": "value" pairs. These are saved with the message and will be returned when exporting the message history. This can make some data analysis easier
recipients.metaDatastringAdditional meta data which can be used to add extra context to recipients
recipients.variablesstringCan contain "key": "value" pairs which can be used in the message body. This allowed a common message body to be personalised for each recipient


In order to shorten a URL within a message, embed [shorten: http://example/longURL.com] into the request "body.text" property. The platform will then automatically convert your long URL into a shortened URL in format uk.endx.io/abcd123. These are unique per recipient. To see an example of this request, see the Request body examples section below. Please note, the shorten URL capability is not available during Trial. You will need to upgrade to a full account to use this feature.

Request body example for rate limit throttled schedule

This configuration allows you to control the rate limit of messages to be sent per hour. The platform will then calculate the estimated end date for the request based on the specified rate limit
{
    "throttleScheduleInformation": {
        "startDate": "2025-07-10",
        "timeSlotStart": "15:51:00",
        "rateOfSend": 100
    },
    "dispatch": {
        "name": "JMclane",
        "characterSet": "Auto",
        "channel": "SMS",
        "from": "JMclane",
        "messageType": "MarketingAndResearch",
        "body": {
          "text": "Your daily reminder: Time to check in! [shorten: http://example/yourbrand/longURL.com]"
        }
    },
    "recipients": [
        {
            "msisdn": "+447741017675"
        }
    ],
    "contacts": []
}


Example Request body for periodic throttle schedule

This configuration allows you to specify the end date required for all the messages within the request to be sent. The platform then determines the optimal rate limit for the request.
{
    "throttleScheduleInformation": {
        "startDate": "2025-07-10",
        "endDate": "2025-07-12",
        "timeSlotStart": "15:51:00",
        "timeSlotEnd": "16:51:00"
    },
    "dispatch": {
        "name": "JMclane",
        "characterSet": "Auto",
        "channel": "SMS",
        "from": "JMclane",
        "messageType": "MarketingAndResearch",
        "body": {
            "text": "Hello from test periodic throttle schedule"
        }
    },
    "recipients": [
        {
            "msisdn": "+447741017675"
        }
    ],
    "contacts": []
}

sections.title: Responses
sections.content:
The standard responses for this API are listed below. For a full list of possible REST API status codes, please refer to this guide.

Success
201 Created
The requested schedule has been created
{
    "data": {
        "throttleScheduleId": "9ecac452-f585-4b1f-be45-7657a8583521",
        "estimatedEndDateTime": "2025-07-10T15:51:00.0000000Z",
        "numberOfRecipients": 1
    }
}

Error codes

400 Bad Request
The server could not understand the request due to incorrect syntax or an incorrect/missing required property. You should not repeat the request without modifications.
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "errorCode": "string",
      "errorMessage": "string"
    }
  ]
}

401 Unauthorized
Indicates that the request has failed due to missing or incorrect authentication information. You can repeat the request with a suitable authorization header field
{
    "errors": [
        {
            "errorCode": "unauthenticatedError",
            "errorMessage": "Request for authenticated route '/api/v2/throttle-schedule' was unauthenticated"
        }
    ]
}
